archetype.name: Fringe Contender (QB-depleted)
archetype.definition: A roster built around Derrick Henry and a franchise quarterback that played like a playoff team when Lamar Jackson was healthy, but now has to tread water with its third-string passer until his mid-December return estimate.

report.headline: A Jackson-dependent team now down to its third quarterback, sliding fast.
report.take:
This Ravens team was built to run through Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry, and for a month it did. Jackson's first four starts produced real passing efficiency, including double-digit pass EPA games against Indianapolis, Dallas and Tennessee, and Henry's workload (175 carries, by far the team's most) gave the offense a floor. Then the quarterback room came apart. Tyler Huntley held it together for a road win in Atlanta before the offense stalled against Cleveland and Cincinnati. Jackson came back for Buffalo and posted -20.2 pass EPA with three turnovers. Joe Fagnano started against Jacksonville and threw for 57 yards with three more giveaways. Huntley is now on injured reserve for the season, and Jackson is on IR after thumb surgery with an estimated return of December 13.

The season-long numbers are an average of two different teams, which is why they look so ordinary. A 19th-ranked offense by EPA and a 20th-ranked net EPA undersell the Jackson weeks and flatter what the offense is right now. The defense needs no such caveat. Its 0.024 EPA allowed ranks 18th, almost exactly where the 2025 unit finished (0.023, also 18th). First-year coach Jesse Minter has not changed the defense's level, and its 26.2 points allowed per game ranks 25th.

The record isn't hiding much luck in either direction. Four wins against a differential that implies 4.8 is close to even, and turnovers are only slightly negative overall. The damage is concentrated: 11 giveaways, a large share of them in the last two games. Around that sit the costs that never show in a box score. Special teams rank 27th by EPA per game, penalties 26th, line penalties 29th, and short-yardage conversion is last in the league. A team without a functioning passer can't absorb those.

The outlook splits in two. Until Jackson returns, this is a run-first team that needs its defense and field position to win ugly. The four-game stretch before his estimated return (the Chargers, Carolina, Houston, Tampa Bay) is soft enough to keep the season alive. The closing division run against Pittsburgh twice, Cleveland and Cincinnati is where a 4-5 team in last place either gets back in it or confirms a lost year.

strengths.title: Henry's ground game travels
strengths.body: Even with three different quarterbacks, the Ravens have run the ball well enough to move it. They rank 7th in yards per carry and 10th in yards before contact, and they put up 172 rushing yards in Fagnano's start. That points to a line that opens the first level on early downs. Because it rests on the line and Henry's workload rather than on Jackson's legs, it should hold up through the quarterback injuries.

strengths.title: Nothing easy underneath or on the ground
strengths.body: The defense is hard to beat with patience. It ranks 4th in explosive runs allowed, 4th in rushing touchdowns allowed per game, and 5th in EPA allowed on short passes. Offenses that want to grind and dink against it struggle. That profile fits the next several opponents, starting with a Chargers offense that leans heavily on a broken run game.

strengths.title: Healthy-Jackson passing was real
strengths.body: Before the thumb injury, Jackson's starts produced pass EPA of 10.3, 11.9 and 12.0 in three of the first four weeks. That level is what a contender looks like. It is the main reason to think the late-season team could look nothing like the current one, if his December return estimate holds.

concerns.title: The passing game has collapsed
concerns.body: The last two games produced pass EPA of -20.2 and -16.7 with three turnovers in each. Jackson was hurt, and then Fagnano, a third-stringer, started. With Huntley out for the year and Jackson on IR, this is the offense until mid-December at the earliest. A pass-protection unit that ranks 29th in pressure rate allowed makes it harder for a backup to survive.

concerns.title: Deep balls and WR1s, now short-handed
concerns.body: The defense is vulnerable down the field. It ranks 26th in deep-pass EPA allowed and 31st in EPA per target to opposing WR1s. The secondary is thinning out: starting corner Nate Wiggins and safety Jaylinn Hawkins are out, and Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a hip injury. This has been a flaw all year, and the injuries make it worse in the short term.

concerns.title: Hidden yards leak everywhere
concerns.body: Several small losses add up. Special teams rank 27th by EPA per game, the team is 26th in penalties, and it converts short yardage worse than any team in the league. None of these depend on the quarterback, so they are the parts the coaching staff can actually fix. They also matter most in the low-scoring games a backup-QB team has to win.

trend.note: A strong start built on Jackson's passing has turned into losses in every game since the win in Atlanta, with the last two lopsided ones coming as the passing game fell apart.

nextGame.headline: Winless Chargers offer a reset, if the backup QB protects the ball
nextGame.body:
Baltimore hosts the 0-8 Chargers as a 5.5-point favorite in a game totaled at 38.5. The Book expects a slog, and the matchup supports that. The Chargers' offense is last in the league by EPA, last in run EPA, and 31st in sack rate allowed. It still has the most run-heavy tendency in the league, which plays straight into Baltimore's best defensive trait. The Chargers' defense is middling at 15th by EPA. It has, however, taken the ball away 12 times, 9th in the league, and that is exactly the danger for a Ravens offense that just gave it away six times in two weeks. On the other side of the ball, the Chargers' run defense ranks 21st by EPA and 23rd in explosive runs allowed, and it has let lead backs beat their averages by more than all but three other defenses. That is a natural target for Henry, and Baltimore gets 11 days of rest to prepare.

Availability shapes both sides. Baltimore's quarterback will presumably be Fagnano again, with Jackson and Huntley both on IR. The secondary is without Wiggins and Hawkins, and Hamilton is questionable with a hip injury. The Chargers list Justin Herbert as questionable with a finger injury that avoided a fracture, and Ladd McConkey is day to day with back spasms. Guard Kayode Awosika is out, a further hit to a line that already allows sacks at a high rate. If Herbert plays at less than full strength, the Chargers' passing game loses its best chance to exploit Baltimore's deep-ball weakness.

waysToWin.title: Feed Henry against a soft front
waysToWin.body: The Chargers rank 21st in rush EPA allowed and give lead backs well above their usual production. Baltimore can lean on Henry, shorten the game and keep the backup quarterback in manageable downs. Even in Fagnano's start, the run game produced 172 yards.

waysToWin.title: Smother a run-first, broken offense
waysToWin.body: Los Angeles passes far less than expected despite having the league's worst run EPA. Baltimore is 4th in explosive runs allowed, so the Chargers' preferred approach runs into the Ravens' strength. Long down-and-distance situations then expose a line that gives up sacks at a 31st-ranked rate.

waysToWin.title: Win the turnover battle by default
waysToWin.body: The Chargers give the ball away often, with a turnover differential of -0.9 per game that ranks 29th. A clean game from Baltimore's offense would likely be enough on its own against a team that has lost every one-score game it has played.

waysToLose.title: Fagnano gives the ball away
waysToLose.body: Three turnovers in his first start and only 57 passing yards are the clearest path to an upset. The Chargers' defense is 9th in takeaways, so it will punish the same mistakes. Short fields would let an otherwise helpless offense score.

waysToLose.title: Herbert hits the depleted secondary deep
waysToLose.body: Baltimore ranks 26th in deep-pass EPA allowed and 31st against WR1s, and it is missing two starters in the back end, with Hamilton questionable. If Herbert is healthy, a couple of downfield completions could be enough in a game this low-scoring.

waysToLose.title: Hidden points decide a rock fight
waysToLose.body: In a game projected around 38 total points, poor special teams, penalties and failed short-yardage tries could swing the result. These have been weaknesses all season.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a run-heavy, low-scoring team until Jackson returns. Henry and the line should keep the rushing numbers respectable, and the defense should stay close to its 18th-ranked level, which it has held for two seasons. Passing efficiency will sit near the bottom of the league with Fagnano. A turnover rate like the last two weeks is unlikely to continue, but the passing game won't be good either. Ranks 32nd, 23rd and 28th on offense make the next stretch the softest available. Carolina and Houston are beatable on the road, and Tampa Bay's offense is weak, though its defense ranks 2nd.

The ceiling depends on Jackson. If he returns on his mid-December estimate and plays near his early-season level, the closing division games against Pittsburgh, Cleveland and Cincinnati are winnable. If he doesn't, those teams are better and healthier, and a last-place finish is the likely result. Baltimore needs to win most of the soft games just to make that final stretch matter.
swingFactors: Jackson's thumb recovery and return date

confidence.note: QB situation unsettled; return estimates aren't promises; small sample with Fagnano.
